<description>
{
 "summary": "Fix four edge cases in P2P opportunistic 1P1C package relay and orphan resolution where peer state collisions disrupt transaction propagation. Prevent reconsiderable package feerate rejections from clearing child orphans across all peers, avoid cancelling txid-based parent requests when a witnessless parent is rejected, track only truly missing parents rather than all inputs for orphan resolution, and stop adding TX_CONFLICT results to reject filters.",
 "problem": "Opportunistic 1P1C package relay and orphan resolution request missing parents by txid while indexing rejections and cache state by wtxid. A peer providing a parent transaction variant with the same txid but a different or absent witness can poison reject filters, cancel in-flight parent download requests from honest announcers, or evict valid child transactions from the orphanage, stalling CPFP packages until a new announcer appears or the parent confirms.",
 "evidence": [
  "PR description: 'A peer sending a variant of a parent with the same txid and a different or missing witness could make the node drop the honest child, cancel the honest peer's request for the parent, or reject later children of that parent. Each case delays a CPFP package until a new announcer appears or the parent confirms.'",
  "Commit c0d03dddb7 notes that ProcessPackageResult passed TX_RECONSIDERABLE to ProcessInvalidTx, which 'erased the child from the orphanage for all of its announcers', even though the feerate failure is specific to that wtxid pair.",
  "Commit d8dc948e13 notes that TX_RECONSIDERABLE clears wtxids from TxRequestTracker across all peers; because wtxid equals txid for witnessless transactions, this 'cancelled every announcer's request for the parent, and the orphan stayed unresolved'.",
  "Commit 3b16af7e7a notes that fuzzing the txdownloadman_impl target without biased operations allowed reverting the witnessless-parent bug fix to survive 57,000 runs unnoticed."
 ],

<category name="p2p" title="P2P">
## Covers

Everything between this node and other nodes: connection management and
peer selection, address management, the message protocol and its
transport (including the encrypted v2 transport), block and transaction
relay including compact blocks, headers sync, transaction request and
orphan handling, network-level DoS protections, and the Tor, I2P, and
CJDNS integrations. The P2P and Private Broadcast labels are a strong
prior.

Not p2p: what the node does with a block or transaction once received
(validation, mempool); RPCs that merely report peer state (rpc).

## What matters here

Resistance to attack first: eclipse and partition resistance, DoS
resistance in message handling and resource accounting, and privacy of
transaction origin. Then relay correctness and liveness: blocks and
transactions propagate reliably and quickly, and nothing gets stuck.
Then interoperability with the rest of the network and with new
protocol features (BIPs) that other software depends on. Then bandwidth
and resource use, which node operators feel. Then connectivity across
network types and platforms.

Protocol changes with a specification and other implementations
waiting rank higher than local optimizations. Refactors count when they
retire a known hazard in message handling.
